name: Hindi Modern
_note: Build this template in week one, not week thirty. Devanagari breaks four assumptions baked into Latin-first typography, and if you discover them late you will be unpicking the engine rather than adding a template. This file documents each one where it applies.
_why_a5: A5 rather than 5.25x8. The wider measure buys back the line length that Devanagari's larger effective x-height and absent hyphenation take away, and A5 is what Indian offset printers quote for by default — imposition is 4-up on a standard sheet, so it is cheaper per copy than a trim they have to make ready for.
_running_head_note: Tracking is 0 and transform is none, unlike every Latin template. Devanagari is a connected script joined along the shirorekha (the horizontal headline); letterspacing severs it and produces something between illegible and insulting. Devanagari also has no case, so uppercase does nothing. The engine's :lang() block neutralises these globally, but templates should not set them in the first place.
_folio_note: Lining figures, not old-style. Old-style figures are a Latin typographic convention with no Devanagari equivalent, and Noto Serif Devanagari does not carry them. Decide separately whether folios use Western (1 2 3) or Devanagari (१ २ ३) numerals — this is an editorial choice per book, not a template one, so expose it in Book Details.

vars._leading_note: 1.85, against 1.42 for the novel template. Devanagari stacks matras above the shirorekha and below the baseline; at Latin leading, the upper matra of one line collides with the lower matra of the line above. This is the single most common defect in Indian-language books produced with Western software.
vars._justification_note: Justified with hyphenation off, because no hyphenation dictionary exists for Hindi and algorithmic breaking of a conjunct produces nonsense. Justification without hyphenation opens rivers on a narrow measure — which is the second reason for A5. Watch this in preflight: if a page shows more than two badly loose lines, the honest fix is ragged-right, so keep body-align switchable per book.
vars._title_leading_note: 1.45 on the title, well above the 1.15 a Latin display line would take. Display sizes make the matra collision worse, not better.
vars._quote_note: Quotations stay at full size and are not italicised. Noto Serif Devanagari has no true italic, and a synthesised oblique slants the shirorekha into something no reader recognises. Distinguish quotations by indent and leading instead.
